---
title: "Quantities not identified by pairwise probabilities"
subtitle: "4.13 · after the postrank theory book, chapters 11 and 25, and vignettes m2/m3"
description: "Limits of pairwise probabilities for composite targets and joint-correctness events."
---

Pairwise probabilities fix a report's additive expected risk, whereas composite directions and joint all-correct probabilities depend on how errors occur together.

```{=html}

```

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Together**: Additive risk and all-criteria correctness are both .500 when the criteria agree across states.
- **Opposite**: Additive risk stays .500, whereas forward composite error and all-criteria correctness drop to 0.
- **Halfway**: All-criteria correctness is .250 while expected wrong count and additive risk remain unchanged.
- **One zero error weight**: Zero weighted wrong count has probability .500, while all-criteria correctness is 0.
- **Select withholding**: Withholding every pair leaves mean accuracy at "NA: no disclosure" with vacuous no-error events.
- **Five statements**: Mean weighted accuracy is .870 across 5 statements vs. .750 all-criteria correctness; in **Data**, state two has 2.600 weighted wrong count.

<details>
<summary>Coupling, composite targets, and scope</summary>

Changing how the two criteria's states are paired while holding each criterion's two-unit distribution fixed leaves every fixed report's additive risk invariant. Joint all-criteria correctness and composite directions still move because composite targets depend on magnitudes and joint events depend on whole-state probabilities. Larger target values indicate higher reporting priority; marginal pair probabilities alone leave joint events and composite posteriors undetermined.

</details>

[Open standalone](../../embed/pairs-leave-open.html), for example `?preset=opposite&theme=dark`.
